statement: By differentiating the identity $(1+x)^{n}=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom{n}{r}x^{r}$ with respect to $x$, obtain the value of $\sum_{r=0}^{n}r\binom{n}{r}$. By differentiating a second time, obtain $\sum_{r=0}^{n}r(r-1)\binom{n}{r}$, and hence show that $\sum_{r=0}^{n}r^{2}\binom{n}{r}=n(n+1)2^{n-2}$.
solution: Differentiating $(1+x)^{n}=\sum\binom{n}{r}x^{r}$ gives $n(1+x)^{n-1}=\sum r\binom{n}{r}x^{r-1}$; multiplying by $x$ and setting $x=1$ yields $\sum r\binom{n}{r}=n2^{n-1}$. Differentiating again, $n(n-1)(1+x)^{n-2}=\sum r(r-1)\binom{n}{r}x^{r-2}$, so at $x=1$, $\sum r(r-1)\binom{n}{r}=n(n-1)2^{n-2}$. Finally $\sum r^{2}\binom{n}{r}=\sum r(r-1)\binom{n}{r}+\sum r\binom{n}{r}=n(n-1)2^{n-2}+n2^{n-1}=n2^{n-2}(n-1+2)=n(n+1)2^{n-2}$.
hints: Differentiate the binomial expansion once and set $x=1$.
Differentiate a second time for the $r(r-1)$ sum.
